title: Integrating Generative AI in Knowledge Building
extended_summary:
This paper examines how generative AI, specifically ChatGPT, can be integrated into K-12 classroom knowledge-building activities and what this integration reveals about students’ emerging AI literacy. The authors focus on a high school World Religions course and ask how students used ChatGPT in their knowledge-building work and how their understanding of AI changed through that experience.

The intervention was a teacher-designed pedagogical approach embedded in an elective high school course. The teacher introduced ChatGPT, modeled its use, and structured student activity in two phases: first, using ChatGPT to generate ideas and questions that students critiqued and built upon; second, using a steering prompt so students could converse with ChatGPT, fact-check responses, discuss them with peers, and incorporate them into group notes and final essays. Students were encouraged to use prompts in English or Spanish, and the teacher provided guidance on prompt engineering, citation, and ethical use. Data came from student interviews, classroom artifacts, and teacher planning/reflection documents.

Findings show that students used ChatGPT in multiple ways: for information search, idea generation, support for writing, rapid access to information during discussion, and brainstorming questions. Students also reported challenges such as hallucinations, limited reliability, difficulty with prompt design, and the need to verify and contextualize outputs. The study concludes that mindful classroom use of ChatGPT, paired with teacher scaffolding and explicit attention to limitations, can support both knowledge building and AI literacy. It also suggests that educators need to create structured opportunities for students to reflect on AI’s strengths, weaknesses, risks, and appropriate use in schoolwork.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI chatbot powered by GPT-family large language models, able to answer questions, generate text, and support interactive prompting/dialogue.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in a high school world religions course to support knowledge building and writing. Students used it for information search, idea generation, question generation, essay drafting, and answering student questions via a teacher-designed steering prompt; the teacher also modeled ethical use, prompted fact-checking, and required transcript citation when used in final essays.

findings.finding_summary: In qualitative interviews with 10 high school students, ChatGPT was used in multiple ways to support knowledge building: 70% reported it improved information-search efficiency, and about 60% used it to keep up with class discussion by getting quick information. Students also reported benefits for brainstorming, generating questions, and reducing workload on writing tasks, but they emphasized that outputs required fact-checking and sometimes led to shortcut use rather than learning.
findings.measure: Semi-structured student interviews; student writing/artifacts; teacher planning/reflection notes

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/mixed-methods single-case classroom study with interviews and artifacts, not an experimental design. It provides implementation detail and observational evidence, but not causal estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived benefits and classroom use patterns rather than measurable learning gains. The evidence suggests useful support for literacy-related tasks, but the impact is unclear and not quantified.
